transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-02 15:30 UTC | Duration: 62m | Host: Samir Patel (Redwood)
Attendees: Samir, Hannah, Diego, Priya - Redwood; Maya, Tom, Nadia, Evan - AegisFlux

Auto-summary: quick alignment on packaging and telemetry. Agreement to run quantization perf pilot.

[00:00] Samir Patel: hey everyone thanks for joining we wanted to combine a couple topics today — packaging for the marketplace listing and then some of the infra and telemetry expectations for private/hybrid installs, and thirdly the quantization bench that AegisFlux asked about.
[00:12] Maya Rodriguez: yep thanks Samir, we have a couple of stakeholders on the call, mostly platform and security. Main thing for us is that listing should not force any network egress and must support our regional key residency rules, also telemetry needs to be GDPR-safe and we want visibility into per-model latency breakdown.
[00:28] Hannah Chu: got it, and just to flag up front our marketplace image is basically a helm chart + OCI artefacts; we recommend a small values.yaml that toggles VPC-only networking, KMS integration, and telemetry exporters. we can share a template after the call.
[00:45] Tom Becker: when you say telemetry exporters what are you expecting? prometheus? tracing? logs?
[00:52] Hannah Chu: yes prometheus metrics, structured traces (prefer open-telemetry), and an optional vector/fluent-bit forwarder for logs. For marketplace we usually include a sidecar config that ships to customer endpoints they opt into.
[01:08] Evan Lu: um we can't accept external endpoints due to policy, so any telemetry needs to be push to our internal collectors only — no SaaS ingestion.
[01:16] Diego Morales: that's fine, the helm chart supports local endpoint overrides — so telemetry target is completely configurable. we also include sampling controls and batch sizes.
[01:26] Nadia Alvi: also need to confirm how keys are managed — we require HSM-backed keys in EU for certain datasets and audit trails for model download/install events.
[01:36] Priya Nair: on KMS, Redwood Private supports customer-managed keys via envelope encryption, and the install process can reference a customer KMS ARN. we'll share the KMS integration doc.
[01:48] Maya Rodriguez: perfect. on the marketplace listing itself, is there a standard set of artifacts we should expect? packaging; licensing; install playbook?
[01:59] Samir Patel: yes — we push a listing package that includes: helm chart, OCI image references, a short reference architecture doc, a quickstart script for private installs, and a compliance appendix with SOC2/ISO pointers. we'll send a sample listing.
[02:12] Tom Becker: cool. now quantization — we want to choose a baseline that balances latency/cost but still keeps quality acceptable. we've seen odd regressions when moving from fp16 to aggressive 4-bit.
[02:24] Hannah Chu: yeah this is where the pilot helps. for most transformer decoders, we recommend starting with 8-bit quantization (INT8 or 8-bit float depending on runtime) for chat workloads, then test 4-bit quantization only with eval sets. Redwood runtime supports both 8-bit and fused 4-bit kernels but tradeoffs depend on sequence length and KV-cache behavior.
[02:46] Tom Becker: do you have empirical numbers? like p50 token latency and cost ratio 8-bit vs 4-bit on an A100 or equivalent?
[02:55] Hannah Chu: we do; for a 2k context chat style workload on an A100-equivalent, 8-bit typically reduces token compute cost by ~1.8x vs fp16, and 4-bit can get to ~2.6x but tail latency increases with longer sequences. we'll share CSV perf results but for short conversations p50 latency is often better at 8-bit due to kernel scheduling.
[03:20] Maya Rodriguez: interesting — so we should pick 8-bit as the conservative default in the marketplace listing and then document how to opt into 4-bit?
[03:28] Samir Patel: exactly. default to 8-bit-quantized model variants for the listing. provide an optional 4-bit build with caveats in the release notes.
[03:36] Evan Lu: are quantized kernels compatible with our on-prem GPUs? some of our fleet are older gen.
[03:42] Diego Morales: good question. kernel availability is hardware-dependent; our runtime has fallback to more portable kernels but performance then falls back. we should capture a matrix in the doc: recommended GPU families for each quant profile.
[03:57] Nadia Alvi: about telemetry again, we need to know what sensitive fields might appear in traces or logs; we can't have PII in telemetry even internal.
[04:05] Priya Nair: agreed — by default Redwood telemetry scrubs request/response payloads. metrics are aggregated counts/latencies. For customers who want more detailed payload sampling, it's opt-in and needs an explicit data handling agreement.
[04:20] Maya Rodriguez: ok that addresses GDPR concerns but need the doc for legal.
[04:25] Samir Patel: we'll attach the telemetry data handling appendix and sample DPA language.
[04:30] [04:30] Tom Becker: switching to listing UX — we need the values.yaml knobs so our ops can freeze networking and KMS at deploy time. can you make those explicit?
[04:39] Hannah Chu: yep we can add clear comments and a sample CI job that validates the ingress is disabled.
[04:45] Diego Morales: also consider including a preflight script that checks node GPU drivers, available memory, and kernel requirements — we have a small bash healthcheck we include in the helm hooks.
[04:57] Evan Lu: preflight healthcheck is important — we want failure-fast so installers can remediate before traffic.
[05:02] Samir Patel: noted. on pilot scope — propose a 2-week pilot on AegisFlux staging with 1 model variant (8-bit default) and an optional 4-bit run for comparison. success metrics: p50 inference latency <120ms for short prompts, median tokens/sec above X, and quality delta <= 4% on our eval set.
[05:25] Maya Rodriguez: what is X tokens/sec? we need concrete numbers to commit resources.
[05:29] Hannah Chu: for the initial pilot let's use benchmark target of 120 tokens/sec per GPU for that model class; exact numbers depend on batch mixing. we'll provide the exact perf CSV.
[05:39] Tom Becker: okay, our staging cluster should handle that — we'll carve out 1 GPU node for the pilot.
[05:44] Nadia Alvi: security checklist — we need audit events for model pull, config changes, and admin logins. can your helm hooks emit such events to our audit log?
[05:55] Diego Morales: yes the installer can call a post-install webhook; we can also emit events to stdout which your log collector captures. we'll include a sample audit mapping.
[06:10] [06:10] Samir Patel: i want to call out marketplace listing gating — to publish we need a packaging review, security review, and a short perf snapshot. that is a lightweight gate and we can do that in parallel with the pilot.
[06:23] Maya Rodriguez: timeline-wise, we want the listing live for internal consumption by end of November. Is that realistic?
[06:30] Samir Patel: yes if we run pilot mid-Nov and final packaging second week of December? oh wait that slips — to have internal listing by end of Nov we need pilot to start next week. Hannah, can you run perf bench earlier?
[06:44] Hannah Chu: I can run an initial 8-bit bench tomorrow but the 4-bit deep bench takes a few days to tune. we'll prioritize the conservative 8-bit numbers for the listing.
[06:54] Tom Becker: acceptance criteria for us: successful helm deploy with VPC-only networking, telemetry routing to our internal OTEL, KMS integration confirmed, and perf numbers from Redwood.
[07:05] Priya Nair: noted, we'll provide the packaging checklist and a values.yaml example showing the VPC-only / KMS toggles and telemetry overrides.
[07:13] [07:13] Evan Lu: quick question on model variants and size — does Redwood marketplace expect you to host the model weights externally or include them in the OCI artifact?
[07:22] Samir Patel: typical pattern is to reference a model registry (S3 or private OCI registry) and provide a manifest with checksums; many enterprise customers prefer runtime to pull from their private registry during install rather than including large weights in the artifact.
[07:36] Tom Becker: we'll want the pull to be done using our registry credentials and a tidy verification step to avoid supply-chain issues.
[07:42] Diego Morales: we support registry auth via helm values for imagePullSecrets and a signed manifest for checksum verification.
[07:50] Nadia Alvi: about supply chain, do you sign the helm chart and OCI artifacts?
[07:55] Priya Nair: we support cosign signatures for OCI and helm chart signing; we'll include examples in the packaging guide.
[08:03] Maya Rodriguez: great. any blockers on our side? I think we can provide telemetry dashboards and the staging node.
[08:10] Tom Becker: i'll send the dashboard exports and open a ticket with infra to provision 1 GPU node for the pilot.
[08:16] Hannah Chu: i'll queue the initial 8-bit perf run and upload the CSV to the shared drive, and start a 4-bit tuning branch but flag that the 4-bit results may need extra iteration.
[08:27] Samir Patel: ok recap of next steps — i'll post the packaging checklist and sample values.yaml, Hannah will run benches, Tom/Evan to share telemetry dashboards and confirm staging GPU, Nadia to confirm KMS/residency guardrails, and we'll reconvene after initial bench.
[08:45] [08:45] Maya Rodriguez: sounds good, thanks everyone.
[08:48] Samir Patel: thanks all, we'll follow up in email and slack and add action items to CRM.
[08:52] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional overlaps, product names may be slightly mis-transcribed (e.g., "Redwood Private" transcribed as "Redwood Privat"), timestamps are approximate and inserted every ~30–90 seconds.
